To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a combination of speech and gesture recognition can improve the recognition of speech commands in the presence of background noise and (ii) that the combination of speech recognition, visual perception, and dialogue management can be successfully used to build systems for natural human-robot interaction.
we have developed a system for natural multimodal interaction between a humanoid robot and a human user.

the combination of a number of state-of-the-art components for audiovisual perception and multimodal dialogue processing allows the development of a robust, natural, and intuitive multimodal human- robot interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of technologies for natural, multimodal human-robots interaction, and the integration of these technologies into an interactive humanoid robot system.
the development of a humanoid robot which is capable of interacting with humans using speech and gestures in a spontaneous, natural and intuitive manner.
the development of technologies for audiovisual human-robot interaction that are robust enough to be used for a real robot in a real-world environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we were able to show that a robot can be made to understand a large number of spoken commands, can be made to react to pointing gestures, and that the robot can be made able to recognize and track a user.

we have built a system for human-robot interaction with the capability of understanding spontaneous speech in German, the capability of tracking and identifying persons, the capability of detecting and interpreting pointing gestures, and the capability to recognize head orientation and head pose.
the presented work is a major step towards the realization of natural and intuitive human-robot interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a system that allows the humanoid robot to perceive humans in its environment in a natural and robust way and to interact with humans in a multimodal way, using speech, gestures, and gaze.
it is now possible to have a natural and robust multimodal human- robot interaction, which is a key requirement for the successful integration of robots into our everyday environment.
we have shown that a robot can be made capable of interacting with a human in a natural way, i.e. using speech and gestures and being able to adapt to the user's needs and preferences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of different modalities can improve the performance of a system significantly.

a humanoid robot can successfully interact with humans using a combination of speech, gestures, pointing, and head orientation, and that the robot can even adapt to its human partners in the course of an interaction.
the integration of the various components into a working system is feasible and that the components can be used for the development of new applications for human-robot interaction.
